6:["$","h2",null,{"children":"What awaits you"}]
7:["$","p",null,{"className":"mt-6","children":"First you arrive, and I will offer you water, tea, or coffee. Then we make ourselves comfortable in the group room/atelier. There you will find a variety of materials: oil pastels and soft pastels, graphite, colored pencils and felt-tip pens, watercolors, acrylic and gouache paints, clay, and much more to let your creativity run free."}]
8:["$","p",null,{"children":"We then start the evening by each of us drawing the frame for this evening on a large sheet of paper with an oil pastel. This is the transition ritual into the creative evening."}]
9:["$","p",null,{"children":"Participants often arrive with an expectation to perform, especially when it comes to painting and creating. But that is exactly the task here: letting go."}]
a:["$","p",null,{"children":"We agree that it is not about making beautiful pictures, and not about judging your own or anyone else's. It is about coming into contact with your inner images, and the pressure to perform only gets in the way. What you create doesn't have to match what you imagine either. It merely represents your inner world symbolically. For that, kindergarten drawings are absolutely sufficient."}]
b:["$","h2",null,{"children":"Opening exercise"}]
c:["$","p",null,{"className":"mt-6","children":"Now we start with a first creative exercise. The aim is to overcome the first hurdle into creating. Here is an example: I introduce a random technique where it is impossible to determine exactly what will come out. This helps to let go of control and the pressure to perform. Everyone takes a small piece of paper in postcard format and scribbles a few first lines with their eyes closed."}]
d:["$","p",null,{"children":"To make the opening exercise as easy as possible, there are more specific guidelines. As soon as something is on the paper, you take different colors and continue working on it. All you need to do is look at what you see on the paper and associate from there. There is no right or wrong."}]
e:["$","p",null,{"children":"To feel comfortable in the group, you bring in what you have created and place it in the circle previously drawn with oil pastel. We hold a first short and always voluntary sharing round. With this, we set the frame for the evening once more and agree that whatever is shown and said here is treated with absolute confidentiality and without judgment. It is never a must to say anything. You always have the choice."}]
